title.en: The World of Metals and Non-metals

text.en: A gold ring shines and can be beaten into thin sheets. Coal is dull and crumbles. Elements can be sorted by their properties into metals and non-metals.

Metals are generally hard, shiny and strong. They are good conductors of heat and electricity. Malleable means they can be beaten into thin sheets, like aluminium foil. Ductile means they can be drawn into wires, like copper. Metals make a ringing sound when struck. This is called sonorous.
Non-metals are usually dull, brittle and poor conductors, such as carbon, sulphur and oxygen. Some are gases, such as oxygen and nitrogen. Mercury is a liquid metal. Graphite is a form of carbon that conducts electricity, an exception.
Metals react with oxygen to make metal oxides. Iron rusts in damp air. Metals react with acids to give hydrogen gas. Non-metal oxides, such as carbon dioxide, make acidic solutions in water.
Copper is used in wires, iron in tools, aluminium in foil and gold in jewellery. Sulphur is used in matches and fireworks.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking all metals are solid; mercury is liquid.

points.en: Metals are shiny, malleable, ductile and conduct.
Non-metals are brittle and poor conductors.
Metals rust or react with acids.
